title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
technique: extra decoding heads on frozen/fine-tuned backbone predicting multiple future tokens, verified via tree attention; typical-acceptance scheme

optimized_metrics.evidence: Minimizing the number of decoding steps to decrease latency directly
it cannot further enhance the acceleration rate. Alternatively, we introduce a typical acceptance scheme that selects reasonable candidates from the MEDUSA head outputs.

MEDUSA-1 ... enabling lossless inference acceleration; MEDUSA-2 needs a special training recipe that preserves the model's capabilities; typical acceptance boosts acceptance rate while maintaining generation quality

headline_claim.text: MEDUSA-1 can achieve over 2.2x speedup without compromising generation quality, while MEDUSA-2 further improves the speedup to 2.3-2.8x.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 3 speedup, Table 4 tokens/s base vs Medusa
App. roofline FLOP/s and operational intensity vs batch size (Fig 17-19, Tables 6-7)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Acceleration rate: This refers to the average number of tokens decoded per decoding step. In a standard auto-regressive model, this rate is 1.0.
metric_definitions.notes: = mean accepted length per step incl. the bonus token

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Overhead: This is used to characterize the per decoding step overhead compared to classic decoding, and is calculated by dividing the average per step latency of the MEDUSA models by that of the vanilla model.
Speedup: This refers to the wall-time acceleration rate. Following these definitions, we have the relation: Speedup = Acceleration rate / Overhead.
metric_definitions.notes: single-sequence wall-clock speedup vs HuggingFace baseline; speed also given as tokens/s of one sequence

load_regime: batch=1 ("In the paper, we focus on the setting with batch size 1"; 'representative of the use case where LLMs are locally hosted for personal use'); batch>1 only via roofline analysis in appendix (batch 1-16+), no serving load
tradeoff_acknowledged: Quality vs speed: typical acceptance threshold eps up raises quality but reduces acceleration; self-distilled models (Vicuna-13/33B, Zephyr) get lower speedup to preserve quality. Larger batch erodes benefit (compute-bound).
hardware: single NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe (training and inference)
